The story uses elaborate metaphors to convey the narrator’s claustrophobia and subsequent wonder: the cabin becomes a “muffige Grab” and a “kleinen Sarg,” while the ship’s engine is the “atmende Herz des Leviathans,” invoking the biblical sea creature. The night sky becomes a velvet curtain whose openings release immense light. These images deepen the contrast between oppressive confinement and expansive, almost transcendent beauty.
